objective: Determine whether any judge-ratings or verdict artifact exists in testbed/, state what that means for every accuracy number this repository has published, and report the honest current accuracy status

rung_triggers.escalate_on: reading the gate shows ratings are meant to be produced by an absent runner, or published numbers appear on an externally visible surface needing correction
rung_triggers.de_escalate_on: the answer resolves to one filesystem fact plus a single file of numbers

coordination.why: The task is an evidence-discipline question. A delegate sweeping for published numbers would return a summary I would have to take on trust, which is the exact failure mode; the whole evidence base is a handful of files in one tree that must be read together
coordination.until: the repo-wide sweep grows past one context, or an independent check requires reasoning separate from the reads that produced the finding

changed.why: The task is an evidence-discipline question. A delegate sweeping for published numbers would return a summary I would have to take on trust, which is the exact failure mode; the whole evidence base is a handful of files in one tree that must be read together

decisions.question: What counts as the measurement artifact, and therefore what does 'no file' mean?
decisions.selected: judge-verdict.json at testbed/ root per measure-judge.py:59; absence verified by is_file(), find, git log --diff-filter=D and git check-ignore
decisions.rejected: Inferring absence from a single ls, which cannot distinguish never-created from created-then-deleted or ignored
decisions.rationale: judge-verdict.json is the artifact (measure-judge.py:59) and it was never written, not merely absent from view: OBS-3 shows no ignore rule matches it, and OBS-2 (never tracked in any commit) with OBS-1 (absent from the tree) corroborate. The schema permits one pointer, so the pointer is the observation that closes the alternative explanation a reader would raise first - that the file exists but is suppressed.
decisions.confidence: high in the verdict file never having existed - confirmed by four independent methods
decisions.recovery: a git commit or a tracked blob naming judge-verdict.json under testbed/ would overturn this and mean the file was created then deleted

decisions.question: Does the unsatisfied gate invalidate the numbers in evaluation/RESULTS.md?
decisions.selected: No. The gate governs one quantity - route accuracy, mode/rung vs oracle - never measured and published nowhere; RESULTS.md's figures are false-trigger and quality figures from run-pilot.py, gated on decided>=min_decided not judge consistency
decisions.rejected: Blanket invalidation of all published numbers because no judge is validated - would discard figures RESULTS.md already scopes with n, caveats and two explicit retractions
decisions.rationale: The gate governs one quantity only - route accuracy, mode/rung against the task oracle - which has never been measured and which OBS-10 shows is published nowhere tracked. RESULTS.md's figures are false-trigger and paired-arm quality numbers from run-pilot.py, a separate instrument whose publishable flag keys on sample size (OBS-9), and OBS-8 records that RESULTS.md already scopes each figure with its n and retracts the two broken ones. The pointer is the exhaustive negative search, since the whole claim rests on a number not being anywhere.
decisions.confidence: high in RESULTS.md containing no route-accuracy figure - read in full, and repo-wide grep returns only unrelated third-party domain facts
decisions.recovery: finding a route-accuracy percentage in any tracked file would make RESULTS.md non-compliant with its own line-8 rule and force a retraction

observations.text: testbed/ contains no judge-verdict.json; full-tree find lists only measure-judge.py, run-bench.py, run-tasks.py, README.md, results/{ask-record,silent}.json, tasks/RT-01..12.json
testbed/judge-verdict.json was never tracked in any commit: git log --all --diff-filter=D returns nothing for it and git rev-list --all --objects lists no such path
no gitignore pattern matches judge-verdict.json (rules cover runs/, results/, *.report.html, .eval-fixtures/ only), so the file is absent because it was never written, not because it is hidden
measure-judge.py with no --ratings writes status=not-measured, accuracy_may_be_quoted=false, self_consistency=null, agreement_with_independent_rater=null and exits 1
run-bench.py --require-gate exits 1 with no verdict file present
run-bench.py --from-results results/ask-record.json prints per-task rows plus 'NO ACCURACY FIGURE REPORTED. judge-verdict.json absent; run measure-judge.py'
even a satisfied consistency gate leaves agreement_with_independent_rater value null with meets_floor false; accuracy_may_be_quoted keys only off self_consistency (measure-judge.py:189)

ultimate-dev/evaluation/RESULTS.md exists and is tracked; it states its own rule at line 8 'If a number is not in this file, it has not been measured'. Its figures are false-trigger (0 of 3 decided) and paired-arm pass/quality counts, each carrying its n; Run A (67% false-trigger) and Run B are recorded as DISCARDED with causes
run-pilot.py:1393 sets publishable = len(decided) >= min_decided, a sample-size gate with no judge-consistency component - the pilot and the testbed gate are separate instruments

repo-wide grep for a published route-accuracy percentage returns only unrelated third-party domain facts (Apollo data accuracy in prospecting refs, medical test accuracy in scientific-critical-thinking); no route-accuracy figure is published anywhere tracked
